children: Nyrstar, owned by commodities group Trafigura, will halt zinc production at its Budel site in the Netherlands from November 30 because operations have become economically unviable, it said on Thursday.
The move follows Nyrstar's decision in September to launch a strategic review of the site, which has been struggling with increasing energy prices and weak market conditions for zinc smelters.
"Market conditions for smelters remain extremely challenging, requiring policymakers to act quickly and decisively to retain strategic processing capacity," said CEO Matt Hadfield.

Nyrstar had previously warned that Budel faced mounting pressure as the Dutch government opted not to include measures aimed at reducing grid costs for energy-intensive industries in its 2027 budget. The company said this left it at a disadvantage compared with industrial operations in neighbouring European countries.
The Budel smelter, with zinc production capacity of 315,000 metric tons per year, suspended operations in January 2024 owing to high energy costs and restarted in May of that year.
Nyrstar said the strategic review remains ongoing and all options are being assessed.
It added that no redundancies among permanent employees are expected as a direct result of the production halt and that the plant and its assets will be maintained safely.
